notes: BACKFILL, reconstructed from the sighted per-case scoring because the run store itself is gone: outputs.run_dir points outside the repository, the container was recycled, and no archival path existed at the time - which is what this row's tooling was added to fix. Correct any of them with a NEW row carrying rescore_of; never edit this one. READ THE TWO SCORINGS AS ONE RUN, NOT AS PROGRESS: 2/10 and 10/23 are the SAME patcher output scored against two different oracle sets. Effective fixes rose from 2 to 10 because 13 new driver-backed oracles made previously unscoreable cases scoreable, not because any patch changed. A ground-truth change of this size invalidates comparison across it; any figure spanning the change must say so. NEFR here is effective fixes over SCOREABLE cases (10/23); over the full 24-bug denominator it would read 41.7%, which is a different metric - state which one. Qualifications in force: no committed lockfile for the target tree, so the dependency set was whatever resolved on the day and cross-run comparison of pass/fail counts is uncontrolled; and no frozen pre-patch baseline was captured, so axis B transitions were measured against an unmeasured starting point. Zero destructive fixes is the one unqualified result in this row.
